statement: The function returns a result r and does not fail. Let n = len(nums). For k >= 0, call k feasible if k = 0, or if there exist an integer S and a sequence of k operations starting from the current interval [L,R) = [0,n) such that each operation uses the current interval and is exactly one of: (a) delete the two leftmost elements, add nums[L]+nums[L+1] to the scores, and set L := L+2; (b) delete the two rightmost elements, add nums[R-2]+nums[R-1] to the scores, and set R := R-2; (c) delete the leftmost and rightmost elements, add nums[L]+nums[R-1] to the scores, and set L := L+1, R := R-1; each operation is allowed only when R-L >= 2; and all k operation scores are equal to S. Then r = max { k | 0 <= k <= floor(n/2) and k is feasible }.
preconditions: nums is a slice of i64 with n = len(nums), 2 <= n <= 2000, and 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < n.
